title: Simulation of extended word RAM programs
statement: Let $W,TW,SW:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be functions, and suppose there is a finite-state Turing machine that, on every Boolean input $x$, halts within some time $t_x\le TW(|x|)$, outputs the binary representation of $W(|x|)$, and uses at most $SW(|x|)$ space. For every extended word RAM program $P$ and Boolean value $fn$, there are a finite-state Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $A$ such that the following holds for every Boolean input $x$, natural numbers $t,f$, Boolean value $v$, and Boolean string $o$: if $P$, run on $x$ with an empty coin sequence and word width $W(|x|)$, halts after $n<t$ steps, touches at most $f$ memory addresses, returns $v$, and has emitted string $o$, then $M$ outputs $o$ when $fn$ is true and the one-bit string $[v]$ when $fn$ is false. It does so in exactly $TW(|x|)+A(t+1)(f(W(|x|)+1)+W(|x|)^2+|x|+1)$ steps and uses at most $SW(|x|)+A(f(W(|x|)+1)+W(|x|)+\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+2)$ space.
